clauses.reason: Executive Order 10843, signed 1959-10-09, creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 ("create a Board of Inquiry"), directs it to report to the President "on or before October 16,1959." and provides that after its report the board continues in existence until "terminated by the President". Three commands result: creation of the board, the report deadline, and a continuing existence that lasts until presidential termination. Later event: Executive Order 10848, signed 1959-10-14, amends the second sentence of the penultimate paragraph of this order. Before the amendment the sentence ends "on or before October 16,1959."; after it the held Federal Register text of EO 10848 gives October 19, 1959 as the report date. The amendment moves a deadline by three days and leaves the creation of the board and its continued existence unchanged (owner ruling 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert); an amended report deadline is not an end. The only own-terms end is termination by the President. No held text records such a termination: a held-corpus regular-expression search for a board of inquiry being terminated returned no match, and the held NMB-style report texts do not cover Taft-Hartley boards. That absence is not proof that no termination occurred, so I disclose it as an open earlier-end candidate; but the evidence does not show an earlier end, and under the owner’s report-deadline ruling an order of this kind that stayed on the books ends on its express revocation. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order. The dossier holds only an American Presidency Project transcription row for 10848 as a located provision, so the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12553 (the dossier’s actor context), whose enacting sentence says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The table (page 11) lists the number 10843 as entry 53 of 64; entry 53 of the aligned subject list is "Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the steel industry", which agrees with this order’s own title, and the table also lists EO 10848 as entry 54 (alignment is by position and a reviewer should confirm it). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10843 creates the Taft-Hartley Board of Inquiry for the 1959 steel dispute; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. The report date was amended by EO 10848 (a later event with before and after text). The own-terms contingent end (termination by the President) is not shown by any held evidence and is disclosed. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) revokes the order and its amendment and is the first end in held evidence.

The dossier lists no conflict and no missing item. An unnamed instrument would not end the order (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments).","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives: creation of the board was performed on issue; the report deadline passed; the clause keeping the board in existence until presidential termination ended with the order on revocation. The order creates no delegation or rule that outlived the board.","savings_check":"No saving language in EO 12553 (held text searched); nothing in the order depends on a separate surviving authority.","scope_check":"The whole order is covered by EO 12553, which lists EO 10843 and its amendment EO 10848 and revokes listed orders and amendments without exception. Inventory is a single clause; the held text shows creation, report deadline and continued existence as its only commands."}

savings.reason: EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The board’s report, any injunction proceeding and any settlement of the steel dispute rest on the Labor-Management Relations Act and on the parties’ acts, not on this order.
